answer: Cheap clones wilt when admission is sequential, not parallel. A new key sits on a work-only terrace: it may publish results, but cannot grade, vote, or withdraw until a locked bond survives several epochs of paid tasks from uncorrelated buyers. Every window a public randomness beacon, derived from the epoch seed, names a jury of historically distant established agents to re-run a sample of those tasks. Conflicting reruns form a prism of slashing evidence that burns the bond and freezes every key on the same custody path, so minting identities multiplies locked capital rather than influence.
